probes.support_reason: NONE under N-4: the canonical_task's own final clause directs that no fragment be written for a language with neither a deterministic end-of-lifetime hook nor a standard scoped construct that invokes an explicit close/dispose, and the frozen rubric lists 'F17.P2-final-clause' among the N-4 probes. Quidra 0.2.0 has neither. (a) No end-of-lifetime hook: a class may declare fields and methods only (grammar.ebnf class_member = field | [ 'override' ] function), and no method name is invoked at the end of a value's lifetime. Refutation witness: a Handle class with a `deinit(int &counter)` method, a value created inside an `if true` block that then ends, prints `released` = 0 - the hook never ran. (b) No scoped-cleanup construct: `defer print(x)` -> error[PARSE_ERROR] Expected parameter name; `with open("x")` -> error[PARSE_ERROR] Expected an explicit type; there is no `using`, `try`-with-resources or `finally` in the grammar. (c) The cleanup action the task names is additionally inexpressible from inside the type, because function bodies cannot reach module-level bindings at all: incrementing the already-declared module-level `released` from a method gives error[UNKNOWN_NAME] Unknown name 'released'. Sub-requirements (2) and (3) alone are expressible, but the mechanism sub-requirement (1) - the cleanup running exactly once and deterministically at end of lifetime - is not, and the final clause governs. Reclamation does occur (managed retain/release), but it runs no user code and is not observable by any conforming program: the language exposes no identity operator, no reference-count query and no finalizer.

probes.support_reason: PARTIAL under P-a (the canonical_task's own clause: 'If the language cannot enforce the private boundary at all, express the nearest standard form and score PARTIAL under P-a'). Delivered: a single unit of code named `util` - a file, which is Quidra's normal grouping construct - containing exactly the two items, an accessible `pub_add(int32, int32)` returning their sum plus secret(), and `secret()` returning 1; and, from outside, the qualified call `util.pub_add(2, 3)` bound to a local and produced, value 6 (verified). Not delivered: 'where the language's own rules prevent secret from being referenced from outside util'. Quidra 0.2.0 has no visibility modifier of any kind - `private int32 secret()` is a parse error, and every top-level declaration of an imported unit is reachable through the alias. probes.support_reason: F-1: all three numbered sub-requirements are delivered - (1) the C standard-library function `int abs(int)` is declared as a foreign function with Quidra's own built-in FFI form `extern int32 c_abs(int32 value) = "abs"` (int32 is the fixed-width type that matches C `int` on this target; the Quidra-side name must differ from `abs` only because `abs` is an absolutely reserved builtin identifier, and `c_abs` is the spelling the language reference's own FFI example uses), (2) it is called once with -3, and (3) the returned C int is bound to an int32 local and produced, value 3. F-2/F-4: no third-party package, no binding generator, no separate build step - `quidra build` alone, linking against the platform C library the frozen recipe already links. F-3: builds and prints 3. F-6: the FFI is documented as a first-class, deliberately narrow facility; no normative prohibition or deprecation sentence applies to it. Evidence that the declaration really binds the C symbol rather than being folded away in source: `quidra llvm` emits `declare i32 @abs(i32)` and `call i32 @abs(i32 %v2)` (the final -O3 binary constant-folds the call to the literal 3, which is an optimization of the linked call, not a substitution of it). Note for the OBSERVATION TARGET (scored by B/D only): the extern declaration states the foreignness, the C symbol and the by-value scalar ABI, but the CALL SITE `c_abs(-3)` is spelled exactly like an ordinary Quidra call - there is no `unsafe`, no `@` sigil and no other marker at the use site, so a reader looking only at the call statement cannot tell the boundary is crossed.
